'''Mark E. Davis''' (born October 14, 1955) is the Warren and Katherine Schlinger [[Professor]] of [[Chemical Engineering]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]]. He is a member of the [[City of Hope National Medical Center]]. He earned his [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]], [[Master of Science|M.S.]], and [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in [[chemical engineering]] all from the [[University of Kentucky]]. His lab focuses on the synthesis of materials for catalysis and biocompatible materials for drug delivery.<ref name="Caltech Bio">{{cite web|title=Mark E. Davis|url=http://www.che.caltech.edu/faculty/davis_m/|publisher=Caltech|accessdate=7 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190414150421/http://www.che.caltech.edu/faculty/davis_m/|archive-date=14 April 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Davis was elected as a member into the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1997, for pioneering work in the synthesis of new catalytic materials. He is the founder of Insert Therapeutics and Calando Pharmaceuticals.{{cn|date=October 2026}}

==Research==
He did his doctoral work with John Yamanis on reactions engineering with annular bed reactors. His academic career started as an assistant professor at [[Virginia Polytechnic Institute & State University]] in 1981 and rose until becoming the Charles O. Gordon Professor of Chemical engineering in 1990. During his time at Virginia Tech, he developed some of the earlier [[Zeolite]] [[molecular sieves]] and increasing the pore size.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Arhancet|first=Juan P.|author2=Davis, Mark E. |author3=Merola, Joseph S. |author4= Hanson, Brian E. |title=Hydroformylation by supported aqueous-phase catalysis: a new class of heterogeneous catalysts|journal=Nature|date=8 June 1989|volume=339|issue=6224|pages=454–455|doi=10.1038/339454a0|bibcode=1989Natur.339..454A|s2cid=34932513}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Davis|first=Mark E.|author2=Saldarriaga, Carlos |author3=Montes, Consuelo |author4=Garces, Juan |author5= Crowdert, Cyrus |title=A molecular sieve with eighteen-membered rings|journal=Nature|date=25 February 1988|volume=331|issue=6158|pages=698–699|doi=10.1038/331698a0|bibcode=1988Natur.331..698D|s2cid=26623258}}</ref> In 1991, he joined the faculty of the [[California Institute of Technology]] and served as the Executive Officer of the department from 1999 to 2004. In 2004 he joined the [[City of Hope National Medical Center]], Comprehensive Cancer Center.<ref name="PNAS Profile" />

In 1995, his wife, Mary, was diagnosed with breast cancer and had to go through chemotherapy. Having seen the side effects of cancer treatment, he decided to do research on molecules that would prevent drug from leaking through healthy blood vessels but would stop at the tumor. His group conjugated [[cyclodextrin]] to the anti-cancer compound [[camptothecin]] to improve the bio-availability and exhibit efficacy in mouse tumor models.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Schluep|first=T.|title=Preclinical Efficacy of the Camptothecin-Polymer Conjugate IT-101 in Multiple Cancer Models|journal=Clinical Cancer Research|date=1 March 2006|volume=12|issue=5|pages=1606–1614|doi=10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-05-1566|pmid=16533788|doi-access=free}}</ref> The compound, [[CRLX101]] is now being tested in clinical trials.<ref name="Science begins at home" /> The cyclodextrin nanoparticles are also being used to encapsulate siRNA.{{cn|date=October 2026}}

He was the recipient of the [[Alan T. Waterman Award]] in 1990. In 1997, he was elected to the [[National Academy of Engineering]], in 2006, to the [[National Academy of Sciences]], and in 2011, the [[National Academy of Medicine]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Mark E Davis|url=http://www.acn.unsw.edu.au/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=164:markedavis&catid=47:vprof|website=unsw.edu.au|accessdate=October 27, 2026}}</ref>

Davis is a member of the American Institute of Chemical Engineers, American Chemical Society, the Materials Research Society, and the American Society for Gene Therapy professional organizations, and of Phi Eta Sigma, Omega Chi Epsilon and Tau Beta Pi engineering honor societies. He was inducted into the College of Engineering Hall of Distinction in 1999.<ref>[https://chemat.engr.uky.edu/recognitions/mark-e-davis Profile], chemat.engr.uky.edu. Accessed October 27, 2026.</ref> 

==Personal==
Davis was born in Ellwood City, Pennsylvania, the son of schoolteachers.<ref name="PNAS Profile" />
Mark Davis is an accomplished athlete and was on a full scholarship in track and field at the [[University of Kentucky]]. He is the 400-Meter World Champion for the 55–59 division. He was also part of the USA 4x100 and 4x400 meter teams.<ref>{{cite news|last=Fesenmaier|first=Kimm|title=Caltech Professor Runs to Victories on the World Stage|url=https://www.caltech.edu/content/caltech-professor-runs-victories-world-stage|accessdate=7 April 2013|newspaper=Caltech News|date=28 July 2011}}</ref>

Davis met his wife Mary, who received her undergraduate degree and a master's of business administration from [[Virginia Tech]], while he was a professor at the same school.<ref name="Science begins at home">{{cite news|last=Gellene|first=Denise|title=Science begins at home|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2007-aug-11-sci-chemo11-story.html|access-date=7 April 2013|newspaper=LA Times|date=11 August 2007}}</ref> She was an accomplished [[flautist]] before being diagnosed with breast cancer. The couple has three children.<ref name="PNAS Profile">{{cite journal|last=Ahmed|first=F|title=Profile of Mark E. Davis.|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|date=Dec 26, 2007|volume=104|issue=52|pages=20651–3|pmid=18093958|doi=10.1073/pnas.0704959105|pmc=2409208|bibcode=2007PNAS..10420651A|doi-access=free}}</ref>
